newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - Dec 18.

text.p: A Wellington nurse was among six Red Cross workers murdered in their beds at a hospital compound in the breakaway Russian region of Chechnya, the Geneva-based agency said. An International Committee of Red Cross spokeswoman said the names of the dead would not be given till their families had been notified. The other victims came from Norway, Holland, Spain and Canada. Page 1.

Three banks dropped mortgages rates on Tuesday night after a cautious Reserve Bank statement, but exporters were knocked by a sharp jump in the dollar. WestpacTrust cuts its floating mortgage interest to 9.95 percent after Reserve Bank governor Don Brash said he expected rates to fall. National Bank also dropped its floating rate to 9.95 percent, and cut its one-year fixed-term rate to 8.95 percent and changed its two- and three- year fixed rates to 9.25 percent. Bank of New Zealand trimmed its variable rate to 9.95 percent from 10.5 percent and said all other rates were under review. The Reserve Bank said it would have preferred a more moderate fall in interest rates in
response to last week's coalition government deal. Brash said the fall in rates on 90-day bank bills was "somewhat excessive". Page 1.

Government plans to replace the unemployment benefit with a community wage or training allowance are at least a year away, according to Employment Minister Peter McCardle. He said that when the "enormous" changes would be made was impossible to say but it was doubtful it would be inside a year. Page 2.

ACT NZ was still considering whether it would support the coalition and was deeply concerned by much of its policy, party leader Richard Prebble said on Tuesday. ACT held a special caucus meeting to discuss the issue on Tuesday and an announcement is expected on Wednesday. Without ACT's support, the government's majority is precarious. The coalition holds 61 seats, while Labour, the Alliance, ACT and United NZ hold 59. Page 2.

Lifting the billion-dollar cap on treaty settlements was largely symbolic and unlikely to have much effect on the cost of clearing Maori claims, Treaty Negotiations Minister Doug Graham said on Tuesday. Page 2.

Brierley Investments said on Tuesday it would nominate director Sir Roger Douglas and executive director Rod Price for positions on the board of Australian media group John Fairfax Holdings. BIL announced it had bought a 20 percent stake in Fairfax on Monday for NZ$506 million. The stake would be increased another five percent subject to Fairfax shareholder

approval. A company spokesman said the Fairfax board would meet on Wednesday to consider the appointments. The market appeared unmoved by the deal, leaving BIL's share price unchanged on $1.28, and the investment has received a positive reception from analysts in New Zealand. Page 13.

Wholesale interest rates should continue to fall in the next few months and trigger ongoing reductions in bank lending rates, according to economists. Bankers Trust said on Tuesday night there was "further scope" for monetary conditions to ease during the March 1997 quarter with short-term rates moving toward 7.5

percent, without the NZ dollar rising. The decline in rates has been slowed because of the risks seen by the Reserve Bank from the new coalition policy agreement. The result was that the Reserve Bank had thrown a "big bucket of water" on how far and how fast interest rates could go down, National Bank chief economist Adrian Orr said. Page 13.

LWR Industries has appointed investment bankers First NZ Capital to find an investment partner for its Canterbury sports clothing subsidiary. "The partner that LWR would seek ideally has international experience in brand management and the ability

to open up distribution opportunities, particularly in the northern hemisphere," the Christchurch-based clothing and textile manufacturer said. The move followed a review of the options for achieving continued growth of the Canterbury group of companies, LWR said. Page 13.

November house sales reached their highest levels since last autumn according to the Real Estate Institute. The median price for houses around New Zealand rose to $156,000 in November, up almost seven percent on the same month a year ago. The median price was up $1,000 over the last month alone. Page 14.
